title: Scaling theory of decoherence in Dicke superradiance
authors: Nico S. Bassler, Julian Lyne, Javier Cuerda
abstract: The survival of many-body coherence depends on the competition between correlation buildup and decoherence. In Dicke superradiance, collective emission builds up correlations, producing a peak intensity scaling as $N^2$ for $N$ emitters. We develop a scaling theory including local dephasing and spontaneous emission and obtain fully collective, partially collective, and independent-emitter scaling regimes. The boundary of the fully collective regime defines a continuous phase transition in a transient observable. Local decoherence can prevent $N^2$ scaling despite increasing $N$.
summary: This paper develops a scaling theory to analyze Dicke superradiance when local dephasing and spontaneous emission are present. It shows that the peak intensity scales according to three distinct regimes ($ eta=2$, $1 <  eta < 2$, $ eta=1$), determined by dimensionless parameters governing decoherence strength. This work is crucial for understanding how environmental coupling limits or modifies collective quantum enhancements in many-body systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the competition between correlation buildup (collective emission) and decoherence mechanisms in many-body quantum systems, specifically focusing on how this affects coherence survival.
main_result: The paper derives a scaling theory showing that the peak intensity of superradiance exhibits three distinct regimes ($ eta=2$, $1 <  eta < 2$, $ eta=1$) depending on the balance between collective and decohering processes.
method: An analytical scaling theory is developed using the large-$N$ limit approximation applied to the dynamics governed by a Lindblad master equation, focusing only on dissipation.
model_or_system: The system modeled is Dicke superradiance involving N two-level emitters. The dynamics are described by a Lindblad master equation incorporating terms for collective emission, local dephasing ($\xi$), and spontaneous emission ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Peak radiated intensity $I(t)$ (scaling as $N^ eta$), the scaling exponent $ eta$, and normalized peak intensity ratios.
important_parameters: The dimensionless scaling variables $g_\xi = \xi / (N\Gamma)$ and $ ar{g}_\gamma = \gamma \ln N / (N\Gamma)$, which govern the transition between regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-$N$ limit approximation to derive mean-field equations for intensive variables, and it focuses purely on dissipative dynamics without unitary evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Dicke triangle dynamics showing decoherence effects, and phase diagrams map out the boundaries between $ eta=2$, $1 <  eta < 2$, and $ eta=1$ regimes in the $( ar{g}_\gamma, g_\xi)$ plane.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical problem (coherence vs. decoherence) to developing the scaling theory using mean-field approximations, deriving the generalized scaling law $I^* \propto N^{ eta(g_\xi,  ar{g}_\gamma)}$, and mapping out the phase diagram showing the transition between the three distinct superradiance regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a quantitative framework for understanding how environmental coupling (decoherence) fundamentally alters collective quantum phenomena like superradiance, extending beyond simple mean-field predictions into scaling theory.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The core physics of the new paper—analyzing superradiance dynamics under decoherence ($\xi$ and $\gamma$) in an ensemble ($N$ emitters)—is directly analogous to studying collective decay processes that are modified by environmental coupling or non-ideal pumping/decay mechanisms.
